facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Chebsaurus algeriensis.
Chebsaurus belongs to the family Cetiosauridae.
Chebsaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
Chebsaurus lived in present-day Algeria during the Callovian stage of the Jurassic period.
facts.quote: It lived in present-day Algeria, in the Callovian aged Aïssa Formation.

facts.statement: Chebsaurus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Chebsaurus was approximately 8 to 9 meters long.
facts.quote: It was around 8 to 9 m long.

facts.statement: The name Chebsaurus means "young man" in colloquial Arabic because the fossils were thought to belong to a juvenile.
facts.quote: The word cheb (شاب) is colloquial Arabic for "young man", as the fossils found were believed to be from a juvenile.

facts.statement: Skeletal remains of Chebsaurus were discovered in the Ksour Mountains within the Occidental Saharan Atlas.
facts.quote: Both skeletons, including cranial material, were found in the Ksour Mountains, part of the Occidental Saharan Atlas (Algerian High Atlas).

facts.statement: The species Chebsaurus algeriensis was named in 2005 by Mahammed et al.
facts.quote: The type species, C. algeriensis, was named in 2005 by Mahammed et al.

facts.statement: A second juvenile skeleton of Chebsaurus is known from the same region.
facts.quote: A second skeleton, also from a juvenile of a similar ontogenetic stage, is also known.

facts.statement: The original description of Chebsaurus gave it the nickname "the Giant of Ksour".
facts.quote: The original publication by Mahammed et al., gave Chebsaurus the nickname "the Giant of Ksour".

rejected.statement: The genus Chebsaurus was described by Mahammed et al. in 2005.
Chebsaurus is the most complete sauropod dinosaur known from Algeria.
rejected.quote: It is the most complete Algerian sauropod known.
